Man. The late 90's when Fallout and Baldur's Gate were coming out was such an exciting time. Black Isle Studios was tearing it up. Fallout 2, Planescape Torment, Icewind Dale, Baldur's Gate. We even got a good Might & Magic or two. I was in Middle School and High School for most of this, and talking about all the new RPGs we were playing at the lunch table, and all the things we discovered is one of my fondest memories.

That really is the problem with old games. Unless you start some sort of book club, but with old games, you have nobody to talk to and get excited about them.
Dungeon Master. Released a couple of months before i was born. Basically my introduction into gaming. Still play 1 and 2 regularly every couple of years.

Final Fantasy III - I have fond memories of playing the English romhack on my Pal Tungsten thanks to the magic of emulation. There's something wonderfully soothing about some of Uematsu's tracks, such as Time Remains; hearing it really takes me back...

The game's story isn't that great, but it pulled me in for quite a long time. The ending's pretty cool- it's too bad hardly anybody's played this one due to its lack of a western release when it initially came out.
Sword of the Samurai, came out in 1989, one year before I was born. Oldest game I still play these days.

So I was born in 1983, this might take a minute...

So there were the first three Ultima games which I actually played and beat around 1999 or so. Hype for Ultima IX was crazy, and I decided I wanted to catch up. Mostly beat them with a walkthrough. I should give them another spin, for nostalgia's sake. But I'm 99% certain they've aged like shit. Even in 1999 they were barely games.

Which compares quite poorly with Wizardry (1981) which I got super into about a year or two ago. It's remarkable how much that game truly set the mold for all RPGs that follow. JRPGs, Dungeon Master/Grimrock style RPGs, Bard's Tale/Might & Magic style RPGs, even the AD&D Gold Box Games borrow quite heavily from Wizardry. And almost all the isometric tactical combat RPGs from the Infinity Engine on through the recent resurgence in games like Pillars of Eternity owe the Gold Box Games for laying down their foundation.

Fuck, now I want to go back and try to beat it again.

Looks like Galaga was 1981. That's a game I played the mother fuck out of as a kid when it came out on NES. I used to see old arcade cabinets, but it's been a very long time since I happened across the last one. Maybe whenever I finally settle down in a house I'll hunt one down.

Looks like RobotWar first came out in 1981. It was a game where you programmed a tank's AI. You mostly just scanned with your radar in a certain arc, told it when to move or rotate, and when to fire. The version I played was on Windows 3.1 though, and it was the first time I ever programmed something. I fucking loved it.

It seems Sinistar came out before I was born too. This is another game I used to occasionally see old arcade cabinets for. The one I remember most was at King's Dominion, an amusement park around Richmond, VA. I don't think it's there anymore. I think I used to see one set up at PAX East in the classic arcade room, but the last few years those were mostly replaced with MAME cabinets or other emulators.

Another arcade cabinet I may have to hunt down one day.
